text.p: LME nickel and aluminium closed on Monday with robust gains, while copper also extended its recent rise. NYMEX crude oil slipped below US21.00 a barrel in early trade, but wheat and gold ended higher.

METALS - Three months nickel finished the kerb at $8,085 per tonne, a rise of $210 on the day, after earlier hitting a high of $8,110. The move was the strongest price since May 30, 1996, when the market hit $8,150, helped by news that unpaid workers at Norilsk Nickel will discuss on March 1 the possibility of taking action to disrupt output.

Aluminium also surged to the highest levels since last June, hitting a peak of $1,661 as technical buying overpowered resistance. The market saw some forward selling and borrowing, which pushed prices off their highs, but it still ended with an impressive $23 gain at $1,654.
Copper also carved out a fresh peak since June 1996 of $2,385, but profit-taking knocked it back on the kerb below $2,375 resistance. Prices finished $7 higher at $2,373.
Most analysts are still bullish of copper in the short-term, with tightness emerging in April dates and analysts point to a target of $2,450 based on a ascending triangle.
Some of the other metals explored higher levels, but failed to sustain them. Zinc touched $1,220, but ended only $5 firmer at $1,216, continuing a consolidation phase.
Lead ended $2 firmer at $671 and tin finished the day $5 higher at $5,985 after briefly looking at $6,020.

GOLD - New York precious metals futures ended higher Monday, led by platinum and palladium, as the complex continued last week's recovery. COMEX April gold ended up $1.10 an ounce at $355.50, but had yet to test Friday's highs at $356.80. April gold's five-day simple moving average has crossed back above its 21-day average for the first time since November 1996, but remains below its 55-day average, with resistance now seen around $360 an ounce, traders said. But physical demand for gold is running at high levels also, as Mid-East and Asian investors take advantage of lower prices.

WHEAT - CBOT wheat futures closed higher on fund buying tied to news U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman warned the U.S. is prepared to restart its Export Enhancement Program to counter European farm subsidies, traders said. Traders said wheat was also boosted by fund buying. Wheat closed unchanged to three cents per bushel higher, with March up two at $3.75.

NYMEX OIL - NYMEX spot crude slipped below $21.00 a barrel Monday for the first time since early August 1996 on technical selling, traders said. April deliveries of West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude dropped around 71 cents a barrel to $20.68. Traders said crude's move was more related to refined product weakness rather than its own fundamentals, although relatively low refinery run rates amid a year-over-year crude stock surplus has weighed on crude.
